chapterSummary: Opens with the central claim of the whole text: the mind precedes and shapes every word and deed, so a corrupted mind brings suffering and a clear one brings ease.
pali: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā, manoseṭṭhā manomayā; Manasā ce paduṭṭhena, bhāsati vā karoti vā; Tato naṁ dukkhamanveti, cakkaṁva vahato padaṁ.
translation: All that we are is the result of what we have thought: it is founded on our thoughts, it is made up of our thoughts. If a man speaks or acts with an evil thought, pain follows him, as the wheel follows the foot of the ox that draws the carriage.

chapterSummary: Opens with the central claim of the whole text: the mind precedes and shapes every word and deed, so a corrupted mind brings suffering and a clear one brings ease.
pali: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā, manoseṭṭhā manomayā; Manasā ce pasannena, bhāsati vā karoti vā; Tato naṁ sukhamanveti, chāyāva anapāyinī.
translation: All that we are is the result of what we have thought: it is founded on our thoughts, it is made up of our thoughts. If a man speaks or acts with a pure thought, happiness follows him, like a shadow that never leaves him.

chapterSummary: Opens with the central claim of the whole text: the mind precedes and shapes every word and deed, so a corrupted mind brings suffering and a clear one brings ease.
pali: Akkocchi maṁ avadhi maṁ, ajini maṁ ahāsi me; Ye ca taṁ upanayhanti, veraṁ tesaṁ na sammati.
translation: "He abused me, he beat me, he defeated me, he robbed me,"--in those who harbour such thoughts hatred will never cease.

chapterSummary: Opens with the central claim of the whole text: the mind precedes and shapes every word and deed, so a corrupted mind brings suffering and a clear one brings ease.
pali: Akkocchi maṁ avadhi maṁ, ajini maṁ ahāsi me; Ye ca taṁ nupanayhanti, veraṁ tesūpasammati.
translation: "He abused me, he beat me, he defeated me, he robbed me,"--in those who do not harbour such thoughts hatred will cease.

chapterSummary: Opens with the central claim of the whole text: the mind precedes and shapes every word and deed, so a corrupted mind brings suffering and a clear one brings ease.
pali: Na hi verena verāni, sammantīdha kudācanaṁ; Averena ca sammanti, esa dhammo sanantano.
translation: For hatred does not cease by hatred at any time: hatred ceases by love, this is an old rule.

chapterSummary: Opens with the central claim of the whole text: the mind precedes and shapes every word and deed, so a corrupted mind brings suffering and a clear one brings ease.
pali: Pare ca na vijānanti, mayamettha yamāmase; Ye ca tattha vijānanti, tato sammanti medhagā.
translation: The world does not know that we must all come to an end here;--but those who know it, their quarrels cease at once.

chapterSummary: Opens with the central claim of the whole text: the mind precedes and shapes every word and deed, so a corrupted mind brings suffering and a clear one brings ease.
pali: Subhānupassiṁ viharantaṁ, indriyesu asaṁvutaṁ; Bhojanamhi cāmattaññuṁ, kusītaṁ hīnavīriyaṁ; Taṁ ve pasahati māro, vāto rukkhaṁva dubbalaṁ.
translation: He who lives looking for pleasures only, his senses uncontrolled, immoderate in his food, idle, and weak, Mara (the tempter) will certainly overthrow him, as the wind throws down a weak tree.

chapterSummary: Opens with the central claim of the whole text: the mind precedes and shapes every word and deed, so a corrupted mind brings suffering and a clear one brings ease.
pali: Asubhānupassiṁ viharantaṁ, Indriyesu susaṁvutaṁ; Bhojanamhi ca mattaññuṁ, Saddhaṁ āraddhavīriyaṁ; Taṁ ve nappasahati māro, Vāto selaṁva pabbataṁ.
translation: He who lives without looking for pleasures, his senses well controlled, moderate in his food, faithful and strong, him Mara will certainly not overthrow, any more than the wind throws down a rocky mountain.

chapterSummary: Opens with the central claim of the whole text: the mind precedes and shapes every word and deed, so a corrupted mind brings suffering and a clear one brings ease.
pali: Anikkasāvo kāsāvaṁ, yo vatthaṁ paridahissati; Apeto damasaccena, na so kāsāvamarahati.
translation: He who wishes to put on the yellow dress without having cleansed himself from sin, who disregards temperance and truth, is unworthy of the yellow dress.

chapterSummary: Opens with the central claim of the whole text: the mind precedes and shapes every word and deed, so a corrupted mind brings suffering and a clear one brings ease.
pali: Yo ca vantakasāvassa, sīlesu susamāhito; Upeto damasaccena, sa ve kāsāvamarahati.
translation: But he who has cleansed himself from sin, is well grounded in all virtues, and regards also temperance and truth, he is indeed worthy of the yellow dress.

chapterSummary: Opens with the central claim of the whole text: the mind precedes and shapes every word and deed, so a corrupted mind brings suffering and a clear one brings ease.
pali: Asāre sāramatino, sāre cāsāradassino; Te sāraṁ nādhigacchanti, micchāsaṅkappagocarā.
translation: They who imagine truth in untruth, and see untruth in truth, never arrive at truth, but follow vain desires.

chapterSummary: Opens with the central claim of the whole text: the mind precedes and shapes every word and deed, so a corrupted mind brings suffering and a clear one brings ease.
pali: Sārañca sārato ñatvā, asārañca asārato; Te sāraṁ adhigacchanti, sammāsaṅkappagocarā.
translation: They who know truth in truth, and untruth in untruth, arrive at truth, and follow true desires.

chapterSummary: Opens with the central claim of the whole text: the mind precedes and shapes every word and deed, so a corrupted mind brings suffering and a clear one brings ease.
pali: Yathā agāraṁ ducchannaṁ, vuṭṭhī samativijjhati; Evaṁ abhāvitaṁ cittaṁ, rāgo samativijjhati.
translation: As rain breaks through an ill-thatched house, passion will break through an unreflecting mind.

chapterSummary: Opens with the central claim of the whole text: the mind precedes and shapes every word and deed, so a corrupted mind brings suffering and a clear one brings ease.
pali: Yathā agāraṁ suchannaṁ, vuṭṭhī na samativijjhati; Evaṁ subhāvitaṁ cittaṁ, rāgo na samativijjhati.
translation: As rain does not break through a well-thatched house, passion will not break through a well-reflecting mind.

chapterSummary: Opens with the central claim of the whole text: the mind precedes and shapes every word and deed, so a corrupted mind brings suffering and a clear one brings ease.
pali: Idha socati pecca socati, Pāpakārī ubhayattha socati; So socati so vihaññati, Disvā kammakiliṭṭhamattano.
translation: The evil-doer mourns in this world, and he mourns in the next; he mourns in both. He mourns and suffers when he sees the evil of his own work.

chapterSummary: Opens with the central claim of the whole text: the mind precedes and shapes every word and deed, so a corrupted mind brings suffering and a clear one brings ease.
pali: Idha modati pecca modati, Katapuñño ubhayattha modati; So modati so pamodati, Disvā kammavisuddhimattano.
translation: The virtuous man delights in this world, and he delights in the next; he delights in both. He delights and rejoices, when he sees the purity of his own work.

chapterSummary: Opens with the central claim of the whole text: the mind precedes and shapes every word and deed, so a corrupted mind brings suffering and a clear one brings ease.
pali: Idha tappati pecca tappati, Pāpakārī ubhayattha tappati; “Pāpaṁ me katan”ti tappati, Bhiyyo tappati duggatiṁ gato.
translation: The evil-doer suffers in this world, and he suffers in the next; he suffers in both. He suffers when he thinks of the evil he has done; he suffers more when going on the evil path.

chapterSummary: Opens with the central claim of the whole text: the mind precedes and shapes every word and deed, so a corrupted mind brings suffering and a clear one brings ease.
pali: Idha nandati pecca nandati, Katapuñño ubhayattha nandati; “Puññaṁ me katan”ti nandati, Bhiyyo nandati suggatiṁ gato.
translation: The virtuous man is happy in this world, and he is happy in the next; he is happy in both. He is happy when he thinks of the good he has done; he is still more happy when going on the good path.

chapterSummary: Opens with the central claim of the whole text: the mind precedes and shapes every word and deed, so a corrupted mind brings suffering and a clear one brings ease.
pali: Bahumpi ce saṁhita bhāsamāno, Na takkaro hoti naro pamatto; Gopova gāvo gaṇayaṁ paresaṁ, Na bhāgavā sāmaññassa hoti.
translation: The thoughtless man, even if he can recite a large portion (of the law), but is not a doer of it, has no share in the priesthood, but is like a cowherd counting the cows of others.

chapterSummary: Opens with the central claim of the whole text: the mind precedes and shapes every word and deed, so a corrupted mind brings suffering and a clear one brings ease.
pali: Appampi ce saṁhita bhāsamāno, Dhammassa hoti anudhammacārī; Rāgañca dosañca pahāya mohaṁ, Sammappajāno suvimuttacitto; Anupādiyāno idha vā huraṁ vā, Sa bhāgavā sāmaññassa hoti.
translation: The follower of the law, even if he can recite only a small portion (of the law), but, having forsaken passion and hatred and foolishness, possesses true knowledge and serenity of mind, he, caring for nothing in this world or that to come, has indeed a share in the priesthood.

chapterSummary: Praises watchfulness over one's own mind as the root of every other virtue, and warns that carelessness is a kind of living death.
pali: Appamādo amatapadaṁ, pamādo maccuno padaṁ; Appamattā na mīyanti, ye pamattā yathā matā.
translation: Earnestness is the path of immortality (Nirvana), thoughtlessness the path of death. Those who are in earnest do not die, those who are thoughtless are as if dead already.

chapterSummary: Praises watchfulness over one's own mind as the root of every other virtue, and warns that carelessness is a kind of living death.
pali: Evaṁ visesato ñatvā, appamādamhi paṇḍitā; Appamāde pamodanti, ariyānaṁ gocare ratā.
translation: Those who are advanced in earnestness, having understood this clearly, delight in earnestness, and rejoice in the knowledge of the Ariyas (the elect).

chapterSummary: Praises watchfulness over one's own mind as the root of every other virtue, and warns that carelessness is a kind of living death.
pali: Te jhāyino sātatikā, niccaṁ daḷhaparakkamā; Phusanti dhīrā nibbānaṁ, yogakkhemaṁ anuttaraṁ.
translation: These wise people, meditative, steady, always possessed of strong powers, attain to Nirvana, the highest happiness.

chapterSummary: Praises watchfulness over one's own mind as the root of every other virtue, and warns that carelessness is a kind of living death.
pali: Uṭṭhānavato satīmato, Sucikammassa nisammakārino; Saññatassa dhammajīvino, Appamattassa yasobhivaḍḍhati.
translation: If an earnest person has roused himself, if he is not forgetful, if his deeds are pure, if he acts with consideration, if he restrains himself, and lives according to law,--then his glory will increase.

chapterSummary: Praises watchfulness over one's own mind as the root of every other virtue, and warns that carelessness is a kind of living death.
pali: Uṭṭhānenappamādena, saṁyamena damena ca; Dīpaṁ kayirātha medhāvī, yaṁ ogho nābhikīrati.
translation: By rousing himself, by earnestness, by restraint and control, the wise man may make for himself an island which no flood can overwhelm.

chapterSummary: Praises watchfulness over one's own mind as the root of every other virtue, and warns that carelessness is a kind of living death.
pali: Pamādamanuyuñjanti, bālā dummedhino janā; Appamādañca medhāvī, dhanaṁ seṭṭhaṁva rakkhati.
translation: Fools follow after vanity, men of evil wisdom. The wise man keeps earnestness as his best jewel.

chapterSummary: Praises watchfulness over one's own mind as the root of every other virtue, and warns that carelessness is a kind of living death.
pali: Mā pamādamanuyuñjetha, mā kāmaratisanthavaṁ; Appamatto hi jhāyanto, pappoti vipulaṁ sukhaṁ.
translation: Follow not after vanity, nor after the enjoyment of love and lust! He who is earnest and meditative, obtains ample joy.

chapterSummary: Praises watchfulness over one's own mind as the root of every other virtue, and warns that carelessness is a kind of living death.
pali: Pamādaṁ appamādena, yadā nudati paṇḍito; Paññāpāsādamāruyha, asoko sokiniṁ pajaṁ; Pabbataṭṭhova bhūmaṭṭhe, dhīro bāle avekkhati.
translation: When the learned man drives away vanity by earnestness, he, the wise, climbing the terraced heights of wisdom, looks down upon the fools, serene he looks upon the toiling crowd, as one that stands on a mountain looks down upon them that stand upon the plain.

chapterSummary: Praises watchfulness over one's own mind as the root of every other virtue, and warns that carelessness is a kind of living death.
pali: Appamatto pamattesu, suttesu bahujāgaro; Abalassaṁva sīghasso, hitvā yāti sumedhaso.
translation: Earnest among the thoughtless, awake among the sleepers, the wise man advances like a racer, leaving behind the hack.

chapterSummary: Praises watchfulness over one's own mind as the root of every other virtue, and warns that carelessness is a kind of living death.
pali: Appamādena maghavā, devānaṁ seṭṭhataṁ gato; Appamādaṁ pasaṁsanti, pamādo garahito sadā.
translation: By earnestness did Maghavan (Indra) rise to the lordship of the gods. People praise earnestness; thoughtlessness is always blamed.

chapterSummary: Praises watchfulness over one's own mind as the root of every other virtue, and warns that carelessness is a kind of living death.
pali: Appamādarato bhikkhu, pamāde bhayadassi vā; Saṁyojanaṁ aṇuṁ thūlaṁ, ḍahaṁ aggīva gacchati.
translation: A Bhikshu (mendicant) who delights in earnestness, who looks with fear on thoughtlessness, moves about like fire, burning all his fetters, small or large.

chapterSummary: Praises watchfulness over one's own mind as the root of every other virtue, and warns that carelessness is a kind of living death.
pali: Appamādarato bhikkhu, pamāde bhayadassi vā; Abhabbo parihānāya, nibbānasseva santike.
translation: A Bhikshu (mendicant) who delights in reflection, who looks with fear on thoughtlessness, cannot fall away (from his perfect state)--he is close upon Nirvana.

chapterSummary: Describes the mind as restless and hard to hold, and urges training it the way an archer straightens an arrow.
pali: Phandanaṁ capalaṁ cittaṁ, dūrakkhaṁ dunnivārayaṁ; Ujuṁ karoti medhāvī, usukārova tejanaṁ.
translation: As a fletcher makes straight his arrow, a wise man makes straight his trembling and unsteady thought, which is difficult to guard, difficult to hold back.

chapterSummary: Describes the mind as restless and hard to hold, and urges training it the way an archer straightens an arrow.
pali: Vārijova thale khitto, okamokataubbhato; Pariphandatidaṁ cittaṁ, māradheyyaṁ pahātave.
translation: As a fish taken from his watery home and thrown on dry ground, our thought trembles all over in order to escape the dominion of Mara (the tempter).

chapterSummary: Describes the mind as restless and hard to hold, and urges training it the way an archer straightens an arrow.
pali: Dunniggahassa lahuno, yatthakāmanipātino; Cittassa damatho sādhu, cittaṁ dantaṁ sukhāvahaṁ.
translation: It is good to tame the mind, which is difficult to hold in and flighty, rushing wherever it listeth; a tamed mind brings happiness.

chapterSummary: Describes the mind as restless and hard to hold, and urges training it the way an archer straightens an arrow.
pali: Sududdasaṁ sunipuṇaṁ, yatthakāmanipātinaṁ; Cittaṁ rakkhetha medhāvī, cittaṁ guttaṁ sukhāvahaṁ.
translation: Let the wise man guard his thoughts, for they are difficult to perceive, very artful, and they rush wherever they list: thoughts well guarded bring happiness.

chapterSummary: Describes the mind as restless and hard to hold, and urges training it the way an archer straightens an arrow.
pali: Dūraṅgamaṁ ekacaraṁ, asarīraṁ guhāsayaṁ; Ye cittaṁ saṁyamissanti, mokkhanti mārabandhanā.
translation: Those who bridle their mind which travels far, moves about alone, is without a body, and hides in the chamber (of the heart), will be free from the bonds of Mara (the tempter).

chapterSummary: Describes the mind as restless and hard to hold, and urges training it the way an archer straightens an arrow.
pali: Anavaṭṭhitacittassa, saddhammaṁ avijānato; Pariplavapasādassa, paññā na paripūrati.
translation: If a man's thoughts are unsteady, if he does not know the true law, if his peace of mind is troubled, his knowledge will never be perfect.

chapterSummary: Describes the mind as restless and hard to hold, and urges training it the way an archer straightens an arrow.
pali: Anavassutacittassa, ananvāhatacetaso; Puññapāpapahīnassa, natthi jāgarato bhayaṁ.
translation: If a man's thoughts are not dissipated, if his mind is not perplexed, if he has ceased to think of good or evil, then there is no fear for him while he is watchful.

chapterSummary: Describes the mind as restless and hard to hold, and urges training it the way an archer straightens an arrow.
pali: Kumbhūpamaṁ kāyamimaṁ viditvā, Nagarūpamaṁ cittamidaṁ ṭhapetvā; Yodhetha māraṁ paññāvudhena, Jitañca rakkhe anivesano siyā.
translation: Knowing that this body is (fragile) like a jar, and making this thought firm like a fortress, one should attack Mara (the tempter) with the weapon of knowledge, one should watch him when conquered, and should never rest.

chapterSummary: Describes the mind as restless and hard to hold, and urges training it the way an archer straightens an arrow.
pali: Aciraṁ vatayaṁ kāyo, pathaviṁ adhisessati; Chuddho apetaviññāṇo, niratthaṁva kaliṅgaraṁ.
translation: Before long, alas! this body will lie on the earth, despised, without understanding, like a useless log.

chapterSummary: Describes the mind as restless and hard to hold, and urges training it the way an archer straightens an arrow.
pali: Diso disaṁ yaṁ taṁ kayirā, verī vā pana verinaṁ; Micchāpaṇihitaṁ cittaṁ, pāpiyo naṁ tato kare.
translation: Whatever a hater may do to a hater, or an enemy to an enemy, a wrongly-directed mind will do us greater mischief.

chapterSummary: Describes the mind as restless and hard to hold, and urges training it the way an archer straightens an arrow.
pali: Na taṁ mātā pitā kayirā, aññe vāpi ca ñātakā; Sammāpaṇihitaṁ cittaṁ, seyyaso naṁ tato kare.
translation: Not a mother, not a father will do so much, nor any other relative; a well-directed mind will do us greater service.

chapterSummary: Uses flowers and fragrance as images for a life well lived, gathering good instead of merely admiring beauty.
pali: Ko imaṁ pathaviṁ vicessati, Yamalokañca imaṁ sadevakaṁ; Ko dhammapadaṁ sudesitaṁ, Kusalo pupphamiva pacessati.
translation: Who shall overcome this earth, and the world of Yama (the lord of the departed), and the world of the gods? Who shall find out the plainly shown path of virtue, as a clever man finds out the (right) flower?

chapterSummary: Uses flowers and fragrance as images for a life well lived, gathering good instead of merely admiring beauty.
pali: Sekho pathaviṁ vicessati, Yamalokañca imaṁ sadevakaṁ; Sekho dhammapadaṁ sudesitaṁ, Kusalo pupphamiva pacessati.
translation: The disciple will overcome the earth, and the world of Yama, and the world of the gods. The disciple will find out the plainly shown path of virtue, as a clever man finds out the (right) flower.

chapterSummary: Uses flowers and fragrance as images for a life well lived, gathering good instead of merely admiring beauty.
pali: Pheṇūpamaṁ kāyamimaṁ viditvā, Marīcidhammaṁ abhisambudhāno; Chetvāna mārassa papupphakāni, Adassanaṁ maccurājassa gacche.
translation: He who knows that this body is like froth, and has learnt that it is as unsubstantial as a mirage, will break the flower-pointed arrow of Mara, and never see the king of death.

chapterSummary: Uses flowers and fragrance as images for a life well lived, gathering good instead of merely admiring beauty.
pali: Pupphāni heva pacinantaṁ, byāsattamanasaṁ naraṁ; Suttaṁ gāmaṁ mahoghova, maccu ādāya gacchati.
translation: Death carries off a man who is gathering flowers and whose mind is distracted, as a flood carries off a sleeping village.

chapterSummary: Uses flowers and fragrance as images for a life well lived, gathering good instead of merely admiring beauty.
pali: Pupphāni heva pacinantaṁ, byāsattamanasaṁ naraṁ; Atittaññeva kāmesu, antako kurute vasaṁ.
translation: Death subdues a man who is gathering flowers, and whose mind is distracted, before he is satiated in his pleasures.

chapterSummary: Uses flowers and fragrance as images for a life well lived, gathering good instead of merely admiring beauty.
pali: Yathāpi bhamaro pupphaṁ, vaṇṇagandhamaheṭhayaṁ; Paleti rasamādāya, evaṁ gāme munī care.
translation: As the bee collects nectar and departs without injuring the flower, or its colour or scent, so let a sage dwell in his village.

chapterSummary: Uses flowers and fragrance as images for a life well lived, gathering good instead of merely admiring beauty.
pali: Na paresaṁ vilomāni, na paresaṁ katākataṁ; Attanova avekkheyya, katāni akatāni ca.
translation: Not the perversities of others, not their sins of commission or omission, but his own misdeeds and negligences should a sage take notice of.

chapterSummary: Uses flowers and fragrance as images for a life well lived, gathering good instead of merely admiring beauty.
pali: Yathāpi ruciraṁ pupphaṁ, vaṇṇavantaṁ agandhakaṁ; Evaṁ subhāsitā vācā, aphalā hoti akubbato.
translation: Like a beautiful flower, full of colour, but without scent, are the fine but fruitless words of him who does not act accordingly.

chapterSummary: Uses flowers and fragrance as images for a life well lived, gathering good instead of merely admiring beauty.
pali: Yathāpi ruciraṁ pupphaṁ, Vaṇṇavantaṁ sagandhakaṁ; Evaṁ subhāsitā vācā, Saphalā hoti kubbato.
translation: But, like a beautiful flower, full of colour and full of scent, are the fine and fruitful words of him who acts accordingly.

chapterSummary: Uses flowers and fragrance as images for a life well lived, gathering good instead of merely admiring beauty.
pali: Yathāpi puppharāsimhā, kayirā mālāguṇe bahū; Evaṁ jātena maccena, kattabbaṁ kusalaṁ bahuṁ.
translation: As many kinds of wreaths can be made from a heap of flowers, so many good things may be achieved by a mortal when once he is born.

chapterSummary: Uses flowers and fragrance as images for a life well lived, gathering good instead of merely admiring beauty.
pali: Na pupphagandho paṭivātameti, Na candanaṁ tagaramallikā vā; Satañca gandho paṭivātameti, Sabbā disā sappuriso pavāyati.
translation: The scent of flowers does not travel against the wind, nor (that of) sandal-wood, or of Tagara and Mallika flowers; but the odour of good people travels even against the wind; a good man pervades every place.

chapterSummary: Uses flowers and fragrance as images for a life well lived, gathering good instead of merely admiring beauty.
pali: Candanaṁ tagaraṁ vāpi, uppalaṁ atha vassikī; Etesaṁ gandhajātānaṁ, sīlagandho anuttaro.
translation: Sandal-wood or Tagara, a lotus-flower, or a Vassiki, among these sorts of perfumes, the perfume of virtue is unsurpassed.

chapterSummary: Uses flowers and fragrance as images for a life well lived, gathering good instead of merely admiring beauty.
pali: Appamatto ayaṁ gandho, yāyaṁ tagaracandanī; Yo ca sīlavataṁ gandho, vāti devesu uttamo.
translation: Mean is the scent that comes from Tagara and sandal-wood;--the perfume of those who possess virtue rises up to the gods as the highest.

chapterSummary: Uses flowers and fragrance as images for a life well lived, gathering good instead of merely admiring beauty.
pali: Tesaṁ sampannasīlānaṁ, appamādavihārinaṁ; Sammadaññāvimuttānaṁ, māro maggaṁ na vindati.
translation: Of the people who possess these virtues, who live without thoughtlessness, and who are emancipated through true knowledge, Mara, the tempter, never finds the way.

chapterSummary: Uses flowers and fragrance as images for a life well lived, gathering good instead of merely admiring beauty.
pali: Yathā saṅkāradhānasmiṁ, ujjhitasmiṁ mahāpathe; Padumaṁ tattha jāyetha, sucigandhaṁ manoramaṁ.
translation: As on a heap of rubbish cast upon the highway the lily will grow full of sweet perfume and delight, thus the disciple of the truly enlightened Buddha shines forth by his knowledge among those who are like rubbish, among the people that walk in darkness.

chapterSummary: Uses flowers and fragrance as images for a life well lived, gathering good instead of merely admiring beauty.
pali: Evaṁ saṅkārabhūtesu, andhabhūte puthujjane; Atirocati paññāya, sammāsambuddhasāvako.
translation: As on a heap of rubbish cast upon the highway the lily will grow full of sweet perfume and delight, thus the disciple of the truly enlightened Buddha shines forth by his knowledge among those who are like rubbish, among the people that walk in darkness.

chapterSummary: Contrasts the fool's short-sighted choices with the slow, real cost they carry, often across a lifetime.
pali: Dīghā jāgarato ratti, dīghaṁ santassa yojanaṁ; Dīgho bālāna saṁsāro, saddhammaṁ avijānataṁ.
translation: Long is the night to him who is awake; long is a mile to him who is tired; long is life to the foolish who do not know the true law.

chapterSummary: Contrasts the fool's short-sighted choices with the slow, real cost they carry, often across a lifetime.
pali: Carañce nādhigaccheyya, Seyyaṁ sadisamattano; Ekacariyaṁ daḷhaṁ kayirā, Natthi bāle sahāyatā.
translation: If a traveller does not meet with one who is his better, or his equal, let him firmly keep to his solitary journey; there is no companionship with a fool.

chapterSummary: Contrasts the fool's short-sighted choices with the slow, real cost they carry, often across a lifetime.
pali: Puttā matthi dhanaṁ matthi, iti bālo vihaññati; Attā hi attano natthi, kuto puttā kuto dhanaṁ.
translation: "These sons belong to me, and this wealth belongs to me," with such thoughts a fool is tormented. He himself does not belong to himself; how much less sons and wealth?

chapterSummary: Contrasts the fool's short-sighted choices with the slow, real cost they carry, often across a lifetime.
pali: Yo bālo maññati bālyaṁ, paṇḍito vāpi tena so; Bālo ca paṇḍitamānī, sa ve “bālo”ti vuccati.
translation: The fool who knows his foolishness, is wise at least so far. But a fool who thinks himself wise, he is called a fool indeed.

chapterSummary: Contrasts the fool's short-sighted choices with the slow, real cost they carry, often across a lifetime.
pali: Yāvajīvampi ce bālo, paṇḍitaṁ payirupāsati; Na so dhammaṁ vijānāti, dabbī sūparasaṁ yathā.
translation: If a fool be associated with a wise man even all his life, he will perceive the truth as little as a spoon perceives the taste of soup.

chapterSummary: Contrasts the fool's short-sighted choices with the slow, real cost they carry, often across a lifetime.
pali: Muhuttamapi ce viññū, paṇḍitaṁ payirupāsati; Khippaṁ dhammaṁ vijānāti, jivhā sūparasaṁ yathā.
translation: If an intelligent man be associated for one minute only with a wise man, he will soon perceive the truth, as the tongue perceives the taste of soup.

chapterSummary: Contrasts the fool's short-sighted choices with the slow, real cost they carry, often across a lifetime.
pali: Caranti bālā dummedhā, amitteneva attanā; Karontā pāpakaṁ kammaṁ, yaṁ hoti kaṭukapphalaṁ.
translation: Fools of little understanding have themselves for their greatest enemies, for they do evil deeds which must bear bitter fruits.

chapterSummary: Contrasts the fool's short-sighted choices with the slow, real cost they carry, often across a lifetime.
pali: Na taṁ kammaṁ kataṁ sādhu, yaṁ katvā anutappati; Yassa assumukho rodaṁ, vipākaṁ paṭisevati.
translation: That deed is not well done of which a man must repent, and the reward of which he receives crying and with a tearful face.

chapterSummary: Contrasts the fool's short-sighted choices with the slow, real cost they carry, often across a lifetime.
pali: Tañca kammaṁ kataṁ sādhu, yaṁ katvā nānutappati; Yassa patīto sumano, vipākaṁ paṭisevati.
translation: No, that deed is well done of which a man does not repent, and the reward of which he receives gladly and cheerfully.

chapterSummary: Contrasts the fool's short-sighted choices with the slow, real cost they carry, often across a lifetime.
pali: Madhuṁvā maññati bālo, yāva pāpaṁ na paccati; Yadā ca paccati pāpaṁ, atha dukkhaṁ nigacchati.
translation: As long as the evil deed done does not bear fruit, the fool thinks it is like honey; but when it ripens, then the fool suffers grief.

chapterSummary: Contrasts the fool's short-sighted choices with the slow, real cost they carry, often across a lifetime.
pali: Māse māse kusaggena, bālo bhuñjeyya bhojanaṁ; Na so saṅkhātadhammānaṁ, kalaṁ agghati soḷasiṁ.
translation: Let a fool month after month eat his food (like an ascetic) with the tip of a blade of Kusa grass, yet he is not worth the sixteenth particle of those who have well weighed the law.

chapterSummary: Contrasts the fool's short-sighted choices with the slow, real cost they carry, often across a lifetime.
pali: Na hi pāpaṁ kataṁ kammaṁ, Sajjukhīraṁva muccati; Ḍahantaṁ bālamanveti, Bhasmacchannova pāvako.
translation: An evil deed, like newly-drawn milk, does not turn (suddenly); smouldering, like fire covered by ashes, it follows the fool.

chapterSummary: Contrasts the fool's short-sighted choices with the slow, real cost they carry, often across a lifetime.
pali: Yāvadeva anatthāya, ñattaṁ bālassa jāyati; Hanti bālassa sukkaṁsaṁ, muddhamassa vipātayaṁ.
translation: And when the evil deed, after it has become known, brings sorrow to the fool, then it destroys his bright lot, nay, it cleaves his head.

chapterSummary: Contrasts the fool's short-sighted choices with the slow, real cost they carry, often across a lifetime.
pali: Asantaṁ bhāvanamiccheyya, Purekkhārañca bhikkhusu; Āvāsesu ca issariyaṁ, Pūjaṁ parakulesu ca.
translation: Let the fool wish for a false reputation, for precedence among the Bhikshus, for lordship in the convents, for worship among other people!

chapterSummary: Contrasts the fool's short-sighted choices with the slow, real cost they carry, often across a lifetime.
pali: Mameva kata maññantu, gihī pabbajitā ubho; Mamevātivasā assu, kiccākiccesu kismici; Iti bālassa saṅkappo, icchā māno ca vaḍḍhati.
translation: "May both the layman and he who has left the world think that this is done by me; may they be subject to me in everything which is to be done or is not to be done," thus is the mind of the fool, and his desire and pride increase.

chapterSummary: Contrasts the fool's short-sighted choices with the slow, real cost they carry, often across a lifetime.
pali: Aññā hi lābhūpanisā, aññā nibbānagāminī; Evametaṁ abhiññāya, bhikkhu buddhassa sāvako; Sakkāraṁ nābhinandeyya, vivekamanubrūhaye.
translation: "One is the road that leads to wealth, another the road that leads to Nirvana;" if the Bhikshu, the disciple of Buddha, has learnt this, he will not yearn for honour, he will strive after separation from the world.

chapterSummary: Describes the wise person's steadiness, and how honest correction from a wise friend is worth seeking out.
pali: Nidhīnaṁva pavattāraṁ, yaṁ passe vajjadassinaṁ; Niggayhavādiṁ medhāviṁ, tādisaṁ paṇḍitaṁ bhaje; Tādisaṁ bhajamānassa, seyyo hoti na pāpiyo.
translation: If you see an intelligent man who tells you where true treasures are to be found, who shows what is to be avoided, and administers reproofs, follow that wise man; it will be better, not worse, for those who follow him.

chapterSummary: Describes the wise person's steadiness, and how honest correction from a wise friend is worth seeking out.
pali: Ovadeyyānusāseyya, asabbhā ca nivāraye; Satañhi so piyo hoti, asataṁ hoti appiyo.
translation: Let him admonish, let him teach, let him forbid what is improper!--he will be beloved of the good, by the bad he will be hated.

chapterSummary: Describes the wise person's steadiness, and how honest correction from a wise friend is worth seeking out.
pali: Na bhaje pāpake mitte, na bhaje purisādhame; Bhajetha mitte kalyāṇe, bhajetha purisuttame.
translation: Do not have evil-doers for friends, do not have low people for friends: have virtuous people for friends, have for friends the best of men.

chapterSummary: Describes the wise person's steadiness, and how honest correction from a wise friend is worth seeking out.
pali: Dhammapīti sukhaṁ seti, vippasannena cetasā; Ariyappavedite dhamme, sadā ramati paṇḍito.
translation: He who drinks in the law lives happily with a serene mind: the sage rejoices always in the law, as preached by the elect (Ariyas).

chapterSummary: Describes the wise person's steadiness, and how honest correction from a wise friend is worth seeking out.
pali: Udakañhi nayanti nettikā, Usukārā namayanti tejanaṁ; Dāruṁ namayanti tacchakā, Attānaṁ damayanti paṇḍitā.
translation: Well-makers lead the water (wherever they like); fletchers bend the arrow; carpenters bend a log of wood; wise people fashion themselves.

chapterSummary: Describes the wise person's steadiness, and how honest correction from a wise friend is worth seeking out.
pali: Selo yathā ekaghano, vātena na samīrati; Evaṁ nindāpasaṁsāsu, na samiñjanti paṇḍitā.
translation: As a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, wise people falter not amidst blame and praise.

chapterSummary: Describes the wise person's steadiness, and how honest correction from a wise friend is worth seeking out.
pali: Yathāpi rahado gambhīro, vippasanno anāvilo; Evaṁ dhammāni sutvāna, vippasīdanti paṇḍitā.
translation: Wise people, after they have listened to the laws, become serene, like a deep, smooth, and still lake.

chapterSummary: Describes the wise person's steadiness, and how honest correction from a wise friend is worth seeking out.
pali: Sabbattha ve sappurisā cajanti, Na kāmakāmā lapayanti santo; Sukhena phuṭṭhā atha vā dukhena, Na uccāvacaṁ paṇḍitā dassayanti.
translation: Good people walk on whatever befall, the good do not prattle, longing for pleasure; whether touched by happiness or sorrow wise people never appear elated or depressed.

chapterSummary: Describes the wise person's steadiness, and how honest correction from a wise friend is worth seeking out.
pali: Na attahetu na parassa hetu, Na puttamicche na dhanaṁ na raṭṭhaṁ; Na iccheyya adhammena samiddhimattano, Sa sīlavā paññavā dhammiko siyā.
translation: If, whether for his own sake, or for the sake of others, a man wishes neither for a son, nor for wealth, nor for lordship, and if he does not wish for his own success by unfair means, then he is good, wise, and virtuous.

chapterSummary: Describes the wise person's steadiness, and how honest correction from a wise friend is worth seeking out.
pali: Appakā te manussesu, ye janā pāragāmino; Athāyaṁ itarā pajā, tīramevānudhāvati.
translation: Few are there among men who arrive at the other shore (become Arhats); the other people here run up and down the shore.

chapterSummary: Describes the wise person's steadiness, and how honest correction from a wise friend is worth seeking out.
pali: Ye ca kho sammadakkhāte, dhamme dhammānuvattino; Te janā pāramessanti, maccudheyyaṁ suduttaraṁ.
translation: But those who, when the law has been well preached to them, follow the law, will pass across the dominion of death, however difficult to overcome.

chapterSummary: Describes the wise person's steadiness, and how honest correction from a wise friend is worth seeking out.
pali: Kaṇhaṁ dhammaṁ vippahāya, Sukkaṁ bhāvetha paṇḍito; Okā anokamāgamma, Viveke yattha dūramaṁ.
translation: A wise man should leave the dark state (of ordinary life), and follow the bright state (of the Bhikshu). After going from his home to a homeless state, he should in his retirement look for enjoyment where there seemed to be no enjoyment. Leaving all pleasures behind, and calling nothing his own, the wise man should purge himself from all the troubles of the mind.

chapterSummary: Describes the wise person's steadiness, and how honest correction from a wise friend is worth seeking out.
pali: Tatrābhiratimiccheyya, hitvā kāme akiñcano; Pariyodapeyya attānaṁ, cittaklesehi paṇḍito.
translation: A wise man should leave the dark state (of ordinary life), and follow the bright state (of the Bhikshu). After going from his home to a homeless state, he should in his retirement look for enjoyment where there seemed to be no enjoyment. Leaving all pleasures behind, and calling nothing his own, the wise man should purge himself from all the troubles of the mind.

chapterSummary: Describes the wise person's steadiness, and how honest correction from a wise friend is worth seeking out.
pali: Yesaṁ sambodhiyaṅgesu, sammā cittaṁ subhāvitaṁ; Ādānapaṭinissagge, anupādāya ye ratā; Khīṇāsavā jutimanto, te loke parinibbutā.
translation: Those whose mind is well grounded in the (seven) elements of knowledge, who without clinging to anything, rejoice in freedom from attachment, whose appetites have been conquered, and who are full of light, are free (even) in this world.

chapterSummary: Describes the arahant, the one who has finished the inner work, as free of craving and fear.
pali: Gataddhino visokassa, vippamuttassa sabbadhi; Sabbaganthappahīnassa, pariḷāho na vijjati.
translation: There is no suffering for him who has finished his journey, and abandoned grief, who has freed himself on all sides, and thrown off all fetters.

chapterSummary: Describes the arahant, the one who has finished the inner work, as free of craving and fear.
pali: Uyyuñjanti satīmanto, na nikete ramanti te; Haṁsāva pallalaṁ hitvā, okamokaṁ jahanti te.
translation: They depart with their thoughts well-collected, they are not happy in their abode; like swans who have left their lake, they leave their house and home.

chapterSummary: Describes the arahant, the one who has finished the inner work, as free of craving and fear.
pali: Yesaṁ sannicayo natthi, ye pariññātabhojanā; Suññato animitto ca, vimokkho yesaṁ gocaro; Ākāseva sakuntānaṁ, gati tesaṁ durannayā.
translation: Men who have no riches, who live on recognised food, who have perceived void and unconditioned freedom (Nirvana), their path is difficult to understand, like that of birds in the air.

chapterSummary: Describes the arahant, the one who has finished the inner work, as free of craving and fear.
pali: Yassāsavā parikkhīṇā, āhāre ca anissito; Suññato animitto ca, vimokkho yassa gocaro; Ākāseva sakuntānaṁ, padaṁ tassa durannayaṁ.
translation: He whose appetites are stilled, who is not absorbed in enjoyment, who has perceived void and unconditioned freedom (Nirvana), his path is difficult to understand, like that of birds in the air.

chapterSummary: Describes the arahant, the one who has finished the inner work, as free of craving and fear.
pali: Yassindriyāni samathaṅgatāni, Assā yathā sārathinā sudantā; Pahīnamānassa anāsavassa, Devāpi tassa pihayanti tādino.
translation: The gods even envy him whose senses, like horses well broken in by the driver, have been subdued, who is free from pride, and free from appetites.

chapterSummary: Describes the arahant, the one who has finished the inner work, as free of craving and fear.
pali: Pathavisamo no virujjhati, Indakhilupamo tādi subbato; Rahadova apetakaddamo, Saṁsārā na bhavanti tādino.
translation: Such a one who does his duty is tolerant like the earth, like Indra's bolt; he is like a lake without mud; no new births are in store for him.

chapterSummary: Describes the arahant, the one who has finished the inner work, as free of craving and fear.
pali: Santaṁ tassa manaṁ hoti, santā vācā ca kamma ca; Sammadaññāvimuttassa, upasantassa tādino.
translation: His thought is quiet, quiet are his word and deed, when he has obtained freedom by true knowledge, when he has thus become a quiet man.

chapterSummary: Describes the arahant, the one who has finished the inner work, as free of craving and fear.
pali: Assaddho akataññū ca, sandhicchedo ca yo naro; Hatāvakāso vantāso, sa ve uttamaporiso.
translation: The man who is free from credulity, but knows the uncreated, who has cut all ties, removed all temptations, renounced all desires, he is the greatest of men.

chapterSummary: Describes the arahant, the one who has finished the inner work, as free of craving and fear.
pali: Gāme vā yadi vāraññe, Ninne vā yadi vā thale; Yattha arahanto viharanti, Taṁ bhūmirāmaṇeyyakaṁ.
translation: In a hamlet or in a forest, in the deep water or on the dry land, wherever venerable persons (Arhanta) dwell, that place is delightful.

chapterSummary: Describes the arahant, the one who has finished the inner work, as free of craving and fear.
pali: Ramaṇīyāni araññāni, yattha na ramatī jano; Vītarāgā ramissanti, na te kāmagavesino.
translation: Forests are delightful; where the world finds no delight, there the passionless will find delight, for they look not for pleasures.

chapterSummary: Argues that one well-lived moment outweighs a thousand empty ones, repeating the formula verse by verse.
pali: Sahassamapi ce vācā, anatthapadasaṁhitā; Ekaṁ atthapadaṁ seyyo, yaṁ sutvā upasammati.
translation: Even though a speech be a thousand (of words), but made up of senseless words, one word of sense is better, which if a man hears, he becomes quiet.

chapterSummary: Argues that one well-lived moment outweighs a thousand empty ones, repeating the formula verse by verse.
pali: Sahassamapi ce gāthā, anatthapadasaṁhitā; Ekaṁ gāthāpadaṁ seyyo, yaṁ sutvā upasammati.
translation: Even though a Gatha (poem) be a thousand (of words), but made up of senseless words, one word of a Gatha is better, which if a man hears, he becomes quiet.

chapterSummary: Argues that one well-lived moment outweighs a thousand empty ones, repeating the formula verse by verse.
pali: Yo ca gāthā sataṁ bhāse, anatthapadasaṁhitā; Ekaṁ dhammapadaṁ seyyo, yaṁ sutvā upasammati.
translation: Though a man recite a hundred Gathas made up of senseless words, one word of the law is better, which if a man hears, he becomes quiet.

chapterSummary: Argues that one well-lived moment outweighs a thousand empty ones, repeating the formula verse by verse.
pali: Yo sahassaṁ sahassena, saṅgāme mānuse jine; Ekañca jeyyamattānaṁ, sa ve saṅgāmajuttamo.
translation: If one man conquer in battle a thousand times thousand men, and if another conquer himself, he is the greatest of conquerors.

chapterSummary: Argues that one well-lived moment outweighs a thousand empty ones, repeating the formula verse by verse.
pali: Attā have jitaṁ seyyo, yā cāyaṁ itarā pajā; Attadantassa posassa, niccaṁ saññatacārino.
translation: One's own self conquered is better than all other people; not even a god, a Gandharva, not Mara with Brahman could change into defeat the victory of a man who has vanquished himself, and always lives under restraint.

chapterSummary: Argues that one well-lived moment outweighs a thousand empty ones, repeating the formula verse by verse.
pali: Neva devo na gandhabbo, na māro saha brahmunā; Jitaṁ apajitaṁ kayirā, tathārūpassa jantuno.
translation: One's own self conquered is better than all other people; not even a god, a Gandharva, not Mara with Brahman could change into defeat the victory of a man who has vanquished himself, and always lives under restraint.

chapterSummary: Argues that one well-lived moment outweighs a thousand empty ones, repeating the formula verse by verse.
pali: Māse māse sahassena, yo yajetha sataṁ samaṁ; Ekañca bhāvitattānaṁ, muhuttamapi pūjaye; Sāyeva pūjanā seyyo, yañce vassasataṁ hutaṁ.
translation: If a man for a hundred years sacrifice month after month with a thousand, and if he but for one moment pay homage to a man whose soul is grounded (in true knowledge), better is that homage than sacrifice for a hundred years.

chapterSummary: Argues that one well-lived moment outweighs a thousand empty ones, repeating the formula verse by verse.
pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jantu, aggiṁ paricare vane; Ekañca bhāvitattānaṁ, muhuttamapi pūjaye; Sāyeva pūjanā seyyo, yañce vassasataṁ hutaṁ.
translation: If a man for a hundred years worship Agni (fire) in the forest, and if he but for one moment pay homage to a man whose soul is grounded (in true knowledge), better is that homage than sacrifice for a hundred years.

chapterSummary: Argues that one well-lived moment outweighs a thousand empty ones, repeating the formula verse by verse.
pali: Yaṁ kiñci yiṭṭhaṁ va hutaṁ va loke, Saṁvaccharaṁ yajetha puññapekkho; Sabbampi taṁ na catubhāgameti, Abhivādanā ujjugatesu seyyo.
translation: Whatever a man sacrifice in this world as an offering or as an oblation for a whole year in order to gain merit, the whole of it is not worth a quarter (a farthing); reverence shown to the righteous is better.

chapterSummary: Argues that one well-lived moment outweighs a thousand empty ones, repeating the formula verse by verse.
pali: Abhivādanasīlissa, niccaṁ vuḍḍhāpacāyino; Cattāro dhammā vaḍḍhanti, āyu vaṇṇo sukhaṁ balaṁ.
translation: He who always greets and constantly reveres the aged, four things will increase to him, viz. life, beauty, happiness, power.

chapterSummary: Argues that one well-lived moment outweighs a thousand empty ones, repeating the formula verse by verse.
pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, dussīlo asamāhito; Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, sīlavantassa jhāyino.
translation: But he who lives a hundred years, vicious and unrestrained, a life of one day is better if a man is virtuous and reflecting.

chapterSummary: Argues that one well-lived moment outweighs a thousand empty ones, repeating the formula verse by verse.
pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, duppañño asamāhito; Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, paññavantassa jhāyino.
translation: And he who lives a hundred years, ignorant and unrestrained, a life of one day is better if a man is wise and reflecting.

chapterSummary: Argues that one well-lived moment outweighs a thousand empty ones, repeating the formula verse by verse.
pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, kusīto hīnavīriyo; Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, vīriyamārabhato daḷhaṁ.
translation: And he who lives a hundred years, idle and weak, a life of one day is better if a man has attained firm strength.

chapterSummary: Argues that one well-lived moment outweighs a thousand empty ones, repeating the formula verse by verse.
pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, apassaṁ udayabbayaṁ; Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, passato udayabbayaṁ.
translation: And he who lives a hundred years, not seeing beginning and end, a life of one day is better if a man sees beginning and end.

chapterSummary: Argues that one well-lived moment outweighs a thousand empty ones, repeating the formula verse by verse.
pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, apassaṁ amataṁ padaṁ; Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, passato amataṁ padaṁ.
translation: And he who lives a hundred years, not seeing the immortal place, a life of one day is better if a man sees the immortal place.

chapterSummary: Argues that one well-lived moment outweighs a thousand empty ones, repeating the formula verse by verse.
pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, apassaṁ dhammamuttamaṁ; Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, passato dhammamuttamaṁ.
translation: And he who lives a hundred years, not seeing the highest law, a life of one day is better if a man sees the highest law.

chapterSummary: Warns against delaying good action and underestimating how small bad habits compound into real harm.
pali: Abhittharetha kalyāṇe, pāpā cittaṁ nivāraye; Dandhañhi karoto puññaṁ, pāpasmiṁ ramatī mano.
translation: If a man would hasten towards the good, he should keep his thought away from evil; if a man does what is good slothfully, his mind delights in evil.

chapterSummary: Warns against delaying good action and underestimating how small bad habits compound into real harm.
pali: Pāpañce puriso kayirā, Na naṁ kayirā punappunaṁ; Na tamhi chandaṁ kayirātha, Dukkho pāpassa uccayo.
translation: If a man commits a sin, let him not do it again; let him not delight in sin: pain is the outcome of evil.

chapterSummary: Warns against delaying good action and underestimating how small bad habits compound into real harm.
pali: Puññañce puriso kayirā, kayirā naṁ punappunaṁ; Tamhi chandaṁ kayirātha, sukho puññassa uccayo.
translation: If a man does what is good, let him do it again; let him delight in it: happiness is the outcome of good.

chapterSummary: Warns against delaying good action and underestimating how small bad habits compound into real harm.
pali: Pāpopi passati bhadraṁ, Yāva pāpaṁ na paccati; Yadā ca paccati pāpaṁ, Atha pāpo pāpāni passati.
translation: Even an evil-doer sees happiness as long as his evil deed has not ripened; but when his evil deed has ripened, then does the evil-doer see evil.

chapterSummary: Warns against delaying good action and underestimating how small bad habits compound into real harm.
pali: Bhadropi passati pāpaṁ, Yāva bhadraṁ na paccati; Yadā ca paccati bhadraṁ, Atha bhadro bhadrāni passati.
translation: Even a good man sees evil days, as long as his good deed has not ripened; but when his good deed has ripened, then does the good man see happy days.

chapterSummary: Warns against delaying good action and underestimating how small bad habits compound into real harm.
pali: Māvamaññetha pāpassa, na mantaṁ āgamissati; Udabindunipātena, udakumbhopi pūrati; Bālo pūrati pāpassa, thokaṁ thokampi ācinaṁ.
translation: Let no man think lightly of evil, saying in his heart, It will not come nigh unto me. Even by the falling of water-drops a water-pot is filled; the fool becomes full of evil, even if he gather it little by little.

chapterSummary: Warns against delaying good action and underestimating how small bad habits compound into real harm.
pali: Māvamaññetha puññassa, na mandaṁ āgamissati; Udabindunipātena, udakumbhopi pūrati; Dhīro pūrati puññassa, thokaṁ thokampi ācinaṁ.
translation: Let no man think lightly of good, saying in his heart, It will not come nigh unto me. Even by the falling of water-drops a water-pot is filled; the wise man becomes full of good, even if he gather it little by little.

chapterSummary: Warns against delaying good action and underestimating how small bad habits compound into real harm.
pali: Vāṇijova bhayaṁ maggaṁ, appasattho mahaddhano; Visaṁ jīvitukāmova, pāpāni parivajjaye.
translation: Let a man avoid evil deeds, as a merchant, if he has few companions and carries much wealth, avoids a dangerous road; as a man who loves life avoids poison.

chapterSummary: Warns against delaying good action and underestimating how small bad habits compound into real harm.
pali: Pāṇimhi ce vaṇo nāssa, hareyya pāṇinā visaṁ; Nābbaṇaṁ visamanveti, natthi pāpaṁ akubbato.
translation: He who has no wound on his hand, may touch poison with his hand; poison does not affect one who has no wound; nor is there evil for one who does not commit evil.

chapterSummary: Warns against delaying good action and underestimating how small bad habits compound into real harm.
pali: Yo appaduṭṭhassa narassa dussati, Suddhassa posassa anaṅgaṇassa; Tameva bālaṁ pacceti pāpaṁ, Sukhumo rajo paṭivātaṁva khitto.
translation: If a man offend a harmless, pure, and innocent person, the evil falls back upon that fool, like light dust thrown up against the wind.

chapterSummary: Warns against delaying good action and underestimating how small bad habits compound into real harm.
pali: Gabbhameke uppajjanti, nirayaṁ pāpakammino; Saggaṁ sugatino yanti, parinibbanti anāsavā.
translation: Some people are born again; evil-doers go to hell; righteous people go to heaven; those who are free from all worldly desires attain Nirvana.

chapterSummary: Warns against delaying good action and underestimating how small bad habits compound into real harm.
pali: Na antalikkhe na samuddamajjhe, Na pabbatānaṁ vivaraṁ pavissa; Na vijjatī so jagatippadeso, Yatthaṭṭhito mucceyya pāpakammā.
translation: Not in the sky, not in the midst of the sea, not if we enter into the clefts of the mountains, is there known a spot in the whole world where a man might be freed from an evil deed.

chapterSummary: Warns against delaying good action and underestimating how small bad habits compound into real harm.
pali: Na antalikkhe na samuddamajjhe, Na pabbatānaṁ vivaraṁ pavissa; Na vijjatī so jagatippadeso, Yatthaṭṭhitaṁ nappasaheyya maccu.
translation: Not in the sky, not in the midst of the sea, not if we enter into the clefts of the mountains, is there known a spot in the whole world where death could not overcome (the mortal).

chapterSummary: Confronts violence directly: everyone fears pain, so cruelty always returns to the one who deals it.
pali: Sabbe tasanti daṇḍassa, sabbe bhāyanti maccuno; Attānaṁ upamaṁ katvā, na haneyya na ghātaye.
translation: All men tremble at punishment, all men fear death; remember that you are like unto them, and do not kill, nor cause slaughter.

chapterSummary: Confronts violence directly: everyone fears pain, so cruelty always returns to the one who deals it.
pali: Sabbe tasanti daṇḍassa, sabbesaṁ jīvitaṁ piyaṁ; Attānaṁ upamaṁ katvā, na haneyya na ghātaye.
translation: All men tremble at punishment, all men love life; remember that thou art like unto them, and do not kill, nor cause slaughter.

chapterSummary: Confronts violence directly: everyone fears pain, so cruelty always returns to the one who deals it.
pali: Sukhakāmāni bhūtāni, yo daṇḍena vihiṁsati; Attano sukhamesāno, pecca so na labhate sukhaṁ.
translation: He who seeking his own happiness punishes or kills beings who also long for happiness, will not find happiness after death.

chapterSummary: Confronts violence directly: everyone fears pain, so cruelty always returns to the one who deals it.
pali: Sukhakāmāni bhūtāni, yo daṇḍena na hiṁsati; Attano sukhamesāno, pecca so labhate sukhaṁ.
translation: He who seeking his own happiness does not punish or kill beings who also long for happiness, will find happiness after death.

chapterSummary: Confronts violence directly: everyone fears pain, so cruelty always returns to the one who deals it.
pali: Māvoca pharusaṁ kañci, vuttā paṭivadeyyu taṁ; Dukkhā hi sārambhakathā, paṭidaṇḍā phuseyyu taṁ.
translation: Do not speak harshly to anybody; those who are spoken to will answer thee in the same way. Angry speech is painful, blows for blows will touch thee.

chapterSummary: Confronts violence directly: everyone fears pain, so cruelty always returns to the one who deals it.
pali: Sace neresi attānaṁ, kaṁso upahato yathā; Esa pattosi nibbānaṁ, sārambho te na vijjati.
translation: If, like a shattered metal plate (gong), thou utter not, then thou hast reached Nirvana; contention is not known to thee.

chapterSummary: Confronts violence directly: everyone fears pain, so cruelty always returns to the one who deals it.
pali: Yathā daṇḍena gopālo, gāvo pājeti gocaraṁ; Evaṁ jarā ca maccu ca, āyuṁ pājenti pāṇinaṁ.
translation: As a cowherd with his staff drives his cows into the stable, so do Age and Death drive the life of men.

chapterSummary: Confronts violence directly: everyone fears pain, so cruelty always returns to the one who deals it.
pali: Atha pāpāni kammāni, karaṁ bālo na bujjhati; Sehi kammehi dummedho, aggidaḍḍhova tappati.
translation: A fool does not know when he commits his evil deeds: but the wicked man burns by his own deeds, as if burnt by fire.

chapterSummary: Confronts violence directly: everyone fears pain, so cruelty always returns to the one who deals it.
pali: Yo daṇḍena adaṇḍesu, appaduṭṭhesu dussati; Dasannamaññataraṁ ṭhānaṁ, khippameva nigacchati.
translation: He who inflicts pain on innocent and harmless persons, will soon come to one of these ten states:

chapterSummary: Confronts violence directly: everyone fears pain, so cruelty always returns to the one who deals it.
pali: Vedanaṁ pharusaṁ jāniṁ, sarīrassa va bhedanaṁ; Garukaṁ vāpi ābādhaṁ, cittakkhepaṁ va pāpuṇe.
translation: He will have cruel suffering, loss, injury of the body, heavy affliction, or loss of mind,

chapterSummary: Confronts violence directly: everyone fears pain, so cruelty always returns to the one who deals it.
pali: Rājato vā upasaggaṁ, Abbhakkhānaṁ va dāruṇaṁ; Parikkhayaṁ va ñātīnaṁ, Bhogānaṁ va pabhaṅguraṁ.
translation: Or a misfortune coming from the king, or a fearful accusation, or loss of relations, or destruction of treasures,

chapterSummary: Confronts violence directly: everyone fears pain, so cruelty always returns to the one who deals it.
pali: Atha vāssa agārāni, aggi ḍahati pāvako; Kāyassa bhedā duppañño, nirayaṁ sopapajjati.
translation: Or lightning-fire will burn his houses; and when his body is destroyed, the fool will go to hell.

chapterSummary: Confronts violence directly: everyone fears pain, so cruelty always returns to the one who deals it.
pali: Na naggacariyā na jaṭā na paṅkā, Nānāsakā thaṇḍilasāyikā vā; Rajojallaṁ ukkuṭikappadhānaṁ, Sodhenti maccaṁ avitiṇṇakaṅkhaṁ.
translation: Not nakedness, not platted hair, not dirt, not fasting, or lying on the earth, not rubbing with dust, not sitting motionless, can purify a mortal who has not overcome desires.

chapterSummary: Confronts violence directly: everyone fears pain, so cruelty always returns to the one who deals it.
pali: Alaṅkato cepi samaṁ careyya, Santo danto niyato brahmacārī; Sabbesu bhūtesu nidhāya daṇḍaṁ, So brāhmaṇo so samaṇo sa bhikkhu.
translation: He who, though dressed in fine apparel, exercises tranquillity, is quiet, subdued, restrained, chaste, and has ceased to find fault with all other beings, he indeed is a Brahmana, an ascetic (sramana), a friar (bhikshu).

chapterSummary: Confronts violence directly: everyone fears pain, so cruelty always returns to the one who deals it.
pali: Hirīnisedho puriso, koci lokasmi vijjati; Yo niddaṁ apabodheti, asso bhadro kasāmiva.
translation: Is there in this world any man so restrained by humility that he does not mind reproof, as a well-trained horse the whip?

chapterSummary: Confronts violence directly: everyone fears pain, so cruelty always returns to the one who deals it.
pali: Asso yathā bhadro kasāniviṭṭho, Ātāpino saṁvegino bhavātha; Saddhāya sīlena ca vīriyena ca, Samādhinā dhammavinicchayena ca; Sampannavijjācaraṇā patissatā, Jahissatha dukkhamidaṁ anappakaṁ.
translation: Like a well-trained horse when touched by the whip, be ye active and lively, and by faith, by virtue, by energy, by meditation, by discernment of the law you will overcome this great pain (of reproof), perfect in knowledge and in behaviour, and never forgetful.

chapterSummary: Confronts violence directly: everyone fears pain, so cruelty always returns to the one who deals it.
pali: Udakañhi nayanti nettikā, Usukārā namayanti tejanaṁ; Dāruṁ namayanti tacchakā, Attānaṁ damayanti subbatā.
translation: Well-makers lead the water (wherever they like); fletchers bend the arrow; carpenters bend a log of wood; good people fashion themselves.

chapterSummary: Reflects on aging and death as reasons to act now rather than keep deferring a meaningful life.
pali: Ko nu hāso kimānando, niccaṁ pajjalite sati; Andhakārena onaddhā, padīpaṁ na gavesatha.
translation: How is there laughter, how is there joy, as this world is always burning? Why do you not seek a light, ye who are surrounded by darkness?

chapterSummary: Reflects on aging and death as reasons to act now rather than keep deferring a meaningful life.
pali: Passa cittakataṁ bimbaṁ, arukāyaṁ samussitaṁ; Āturaṁ bahusaṅkappaṁ, yassa natthi dhuvaṁ ṭhiti.
translation: Look at this dressed-up lump, covered with wounds, joined together, sickly, full of many thoughts, which has no strength, no hold!

chapterSummary: Reflects on aging and death as reasons to act now rather than keep deferring a meaningful life.
pali: Parijiṇṇamidaṁ rūpaṁ, roganīḷaṁ pabhaṅguraṁ; Bhijjati pūtisandeho, maraṇantañhi jīvitaṁ.
translation: This body is wasted, full of sickness, and frail; this heap of corruption breaks to pieces, life indeed ends in death.

chapterSummary: Reflects on aging and death as reasons to act now rather than keep deferring a meaningful life.
pali: Yānimāni apatthāni, alābūneva sārade; Kāpotakāni aṭṭhīni, tāni disvāna kā rati.
translation: Those white bones, like gourds thrown away in the autumn, what pleasure is there in looking at them?

chapterSummary: Reflects on aging and death as reasons to act now rather than keep deferring a meaningful life.
pali: Aṭṭhīnaṁ nagaraṁ kataṁ, maṁsalohitalepanaṁ; Yattha jarā ca maccu ca, māno makkho ca ohito.
translation: After a stronghold has been made of the bones, it is covered with flesh and blood, and there dwell in it old age and death, pride and deceit.

chapterSummary: Reflects on aging and death as reasons to act now rather than keep deferring a meaningful life.
pali: Jīranti ve rājarathā sucittā, Atho sarīrampi jaraṁ upeti; Satañca dhammo na jaraṁ upeti, Santo have sabbhi pavedayanti.
translation: The brilliant chariots of kings are destroyed, the body also approaches destruction, but the virtue of good people never approaches destruction,--thus do the good say to the good.

chapterSummary: Reflects on aging and death as reasons to act now rather than keep deferring a meaningful life.
pali: Appassutāyaṁ puriso, balībaddhova jīrati; Maṁsāni tassa vaḍḍhanti, paññā tassa na vaḍḍhati.
translation: A man who has learnt little, grows old like an ox; his flesh grows, but his knowledge does not grow.

chapterSummary: Reflects on aging and death as reasons to act now rather than keep deferring a meaningful life.
pali: Anekajātisaṁsāraṁ, sandhāvissaṁ anibbisaṁ; Gahakāraṁ gavesanto, dukkhā jāti punappunaṁ.
translation: Looking for the maker of this tabernacle, I shall have to run through a course of many births, so long as I do not find (him); and painful is birth again and again. But now, maker of the tabernacle, thou hast been seen; thou shalt not make up this tabernacle again. All thy rafters are broken, thy ridge-pole is sundered; the mind, approaching the Eternal (visankhara, nirvana), has attained to the extinction of all desires.

chapterSummary: Reflects on aging and death as reasons to act now rather than keep deferring a meaningful life.
pali: Gahakāraka diṭṭhosi, puna gehaṁ na kāhasi; Sabbā te phāsukā bhaggā, gahakūṭaṁ visaṅkhataṁ; Visaṅkhāragataṁ cittaṁ, taṇhānaṁ khayamajjhagā.
translation: Looking for the maker of this tabernacle, I shall have to run through a course of many births, so long as I do not find (him); and painful is birth again and again. But now, maker of the tabernacle, thou hast been seen; thou shalt not make up this tabernacle again. All thy rafters are broken, thy ridge-pole is sundered; the mind, approaching the Eternal (visankhara, nirvana), has attained to the extinction of all desires.

chapterSummary: Reflects on aging and death as reasons to act now rather than keep deferring a meaningful life.
pali: Acaritvā brahmacariyaṁ, aladdhā yobbane dhanaṁ; Jiṇṇakoñcāva jhāyanti, khīṇamaccheva pallale.
translation: Men who have not observed proper discipline, and have not gained treasure in their youth, perish like old herons in a lake without fish.

chapterSummary: Reflects on aging and death as reasons to act now rather than keep deferring a meaningful life.
pali: Acaritvā brahmacariyaṁ, aladdhā yobbane dhanaṁ; Senti cāpātikhīṇāva, purāṇāni anutthunaṁ.
translation: Men who have not observed proper discipline, and have not gained treasure in their youth, lie, like broken bows, sighing after the past.

chapterSummary: Turns attention inward, arguing that no one can protect or improve you the way your own discipline can.
pali: Attānañce piyaṁ jaññā, rakkheyya naṁ surakkhitaṁ; Tiṇṇaṁ aññataraṁ yāmaṁ, paṭijaggeyya paṇḍito.
translation: If a man hold himself dear, let him watch himself carefully; during one at least out of the three watches a wise man should be watchful.

chapterSummary: Turns attention inward, arguing that no one can protect or improve you the way your own discipline can.
pali: Attānameva paṭhamaṁ, patirūpe nivesaye; Athaññamanusāseyya, na kilisseyya paṇḍito.
translation: Let each man direct himself first to what is proper, then let him teach others; thus a wise man will not suffer.

chapterSummary: Turns attention inward, arguing that no one can protect or improve you the way your own discipline can.
pali: Attānañce tathā kayirā, yathāññamanusāsati; Sudanto vata dametha, attā hi kira duddamo.
translation: If a man make himself as he teaches others to be, then, being himself well subdued, he may subdue (others); one's own self is indeed difficult to subdue.

chapterSummary: Turns attention inward, arguing that no one can protect or improve you the way your own discipline can.
pali: Attā hi attano nātho, ko hi nātho paro siyā; Attanā hi sudantena, nāthaṁ labhati dullabhaṁ.
translation: Self is the lord of self, who else could be the lord? With self well subdued, a man finds a lord such as few can find.

chapterSummary: Turns attention inward, arguing that no one can protect or improve you the way your own discipline can.
pali: Attanā hi kataṁ pāpaṁ, Attajaṁ attasambhavaṁ; Abhimatthati dummedhaṁ, Vajiraṁvasmamayaṁ maṇiṁ.
translation: The evil done by oneself, self-begotten, self-bred, crushes the foolish, as a diamond breaks a precious stone.

chapterSummary: Turns attention inward, arguing that no one can protect or improve you the way your own discipline can.
pali: Yassa accantadussilyaṁ, māluvā sālamivotthataṁ; Karoti so tathattānaṁ, yathā naṁ icchatī diso.
translation: He whose wickedness is very great brings himself down to that state where his enemy wishes him to be, as a creeper does with the tree which it surrounds.

chapterSummary: Turns attention inward, arguing that no one can protect or improve you the way your own discipline can.
pali: Sukarāni asādhūni, attano ahitāni ca; Yaṁ ve hitañca sādhuñca, taṁ ve paramadukkaraṁ.
translation: Bad deeds, and deeds hurtful to ourselves, are easy to do; what is beneficial and good, that is very difficult to do.

chapterSummary: Turns attention inward, arguing that no one can protect or improve you the way your own discipline can.
pali: Yo sāsanaṁ arahataṁ, ariyānaṁ dhammajīvinaṁ; Paṭikkosati dummedho, diṭṭhiṁ nissāya pāpikaṁ; Phalāni kaṭṭhakasseva, attaghātāya phallati.
translation: The foolish man who scorns the rule of the venerable (Arahat), of the elect (Ariya), of the virtuous, and follows false doctrine, he bears fruit to his own destruction, like the fruits of the Katthaka reed.

chapterSummary: Turns attention inward, arguing that no one can protect or improve you the way your own discipline can.
pali: Attanā hi kataṁ pāpaṁ, attanā saṅkilissati; Attanā akataṁ pāpaṁ, attanāva visujjhati; Suddhī asuddhi paccattaṁ, nāñño aññaṁ visodhaye.
translation: By oneself the evil is done, by oneself one suffers; by oneself evil is left undone, by oneself one is purified. Purity and impurity belong to oneself, no one can purify another.

chapterSummary: Turns attention inward, arguing that no one can protect or improve you the way your own discipline can.
pali: Attadatthaṁ paratthena, bahunāpi na hāpaye; Attadatthamabhiññāya, sadatthapasuto siyā.
translation: Let no one forget his own duty for the sake of another's, however great; let a man, after he has discerned his own duty, be always attentive to his duty.

chapterSummary: Steps back to survey ordinary life and its illusions, urging a clearer, less self-deceived way of seeing it.
pali: Hīnaṁ dhammaṁ na seveyya, pamādena na saṁvase; Micchādiṭṭhiṁ na seveyya, na siyā lokavaḍḍhano.
translation: Do not follow the evil law! Do not live on in thoughtlessness! Do not follow false doctrine! Be not a friend of the world.

chapterSummary: Steps back to survey ordinary life and its illusions, urging a clearer, less self-deceived way of seeing it.
pali: Uttiṭṭhe nappamajjeyya, dhammaṁ sucaritaṁ care; Dhammacārī sukhaṁ seti, asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.
translation: Rouse thyself! do not be idle! Follow the law of virtue! The virtuous rests in bliss in this world and in the next.

chapterSummary: Steps back to survey ordinary life and its illusions, urging a clearer, less self-deceived way of seeing it.
pali: Dhammaṁ care sucaritaṁ, na naṁ duccaritaṁ care; Dhammacārī sukhaṁ seti, asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.
translation: Follow the law of virtue; do not follow that of sin. The virtuous rests in bliss in this world and in the next.

chapterSummary: Steps back to survey ordinary life and its illusions, urging a clearer, less self-deceived way of seeing it.
pali: Yathā pubbuḷakaṁ passe, yathā passe marīcikaṁ; Evaṁ lokaṁ avekkhantaṁ, maccurājā na passati.
translation: Look upon the world as a bubble, look upon it as a mirage: the king of death does not see him who thus looks down upon the world.

chapterSummary: Steps back to survey ordinary life and its illusions, urging a clearer, less self-deceived way of seeing it.
pali: Etha passathimaṁ lokaṁ, cittaṁ rājarathūpamaṁ; Yattha bālā visīdanti, natthi saṅgo vijānataṁ.
translation: Come, look at this glittering world, like unto a royal chariot; the foolish are immersed in it, but the wise do not touch it.

chapterSummary: Steps back to survey ordinary life and its illusions, urging a clearer, less self-deceived way of seeing it.
pali: Yo ca pubbe pamajjitvā, pacchā so nappamajjati; Somaṁ lokaṁ pabhāseti, abbhā muttova candimā.
translation: He who formerly was reckless and afterwards became sober, brightens up this world, like the moon when freed from clouds.

chapterSummary: Steps back to survey ordinary life and its illusions, urging a clearer, less self-deceived way of seeing it.
pali: Yassa pāpaṁ kataṁ kammaṁ, kusalena pidhīyati; Somaṁ lokaṁ pabhāseti, abbhā muttova candimā.
translation: He whose evil deeds are covered by good deeds, brightens up this world, like the moon when freed from clouds.

chapterSummary: Steps back to survey ordinary life and its illusions, urging a clearer, less self-deceived way of seeing it.
pali: Andhabhūto ayaṁ loko, tanukettha vipassati; Sakuṇo jālamuttova, appo saggāya gacchati.
translation: This world is dark, few only can see here; a few only go to heaven, like birds escaped from the net.

chapterSummary: Steps back to survey ordinary life and its illusions, urging a clearer, less self-deceived way of seeing it.
pali: Haṁsādiccapathe yanti, ākāse yanti iddhiyā; Nīyanti dhīrā lokamhā, jetvā māraṁ savāhiniṁ.
translation: The swans go on the path of the sun, they go through the ether by means of their miraculous power; the wise are led out of this world, when they have conquered Mara and his train.

chapterSummary: Steps back to survey ordinary life and its illusions, urging a clearer, less self-deceived way of seeing it.
pali: Ekaṁ dhammaṁ atītassa, musāvādissa jantuno; Vitiṇṇaparalokassa, natthi pāpaṁ akāriyaṁ.
translation: If a man has transgressed one law, and speaks lies, and scoffs at another world, there is no evil he will not do.

chapterSummary: Steps back to survey ordinary life and its illusions, urging a clearer, less self-deceived way of seeing it.
pali: Na ve kadariyā devalokaṁ vajanti, Bālā have nappasaṁsanti dānaṁ; Dhīro ca dānaṁ anumodamāno, Teneva so hoti sukhī parattha.
translation: The uncharitable do not go to the world of the gods; fools only do not praise liberality; a wise man rejoices in liberality, and through it becomes blessed in the other world.

chapterSummary: Steps back to survey ordinary life and its illusions, urging a clearer, less self-deceived way of seeing it.
pali: Pathabyā ekarajjena, saggassa gamanena vā; Sabbalokādhipaccena, sotāpattiphalaṁ varaṁ.
translation: Better than sovereignty over the earth, better than going to heaven, better than lordship over all worlds, is the reward of the first step in holiness.

chapterSummary: Describes the Buddha's own nature and the kind of clarity that makes someone worth learning from.
pali: Yassa jitaṁ nāvajīyati, Jitaṁ yassa noyāti koci loke; Taṁ buddhamanantagocaraṁ, Apadaṁ kena padena nessatha.
translation: He whose conquest is not conquered again, into whose conquest no one in this world enters, by what track can you lead him, the Awakened, the Omniscient, the trackless?

chapterSummary: Describes the Buddha's own nature and the kind of clarity that makes someone worth learning from.
pali: Yassa jālinī visattikā, Taṇhā natthi kuhiñci netave; Taṁ buddhamanantagocaraṁ, Apadaṁ kena padena nessatha.
translation: He whom no desire with its snares and poisons can lead astray, by what track can you lead him, the Awakened, the Omniscient, the trackless?

chapterSummary: Describes the Buddha's own nature and the kind of clarity that makes someone worth learning from.
pali: Ye jhānapasutā dhīrā, nekkhammūpasame ratā; Devāpi tesaṁ pihayanti, sambuddhānaṁ satīmataṁ.
translation: Even the gods envy those who are awakened and not forgetful, who are given to meditation, who are wise, and who delight in the repose of retirement (from the world).

chapterSummary: Describes the Buddha's own nature and the kind of clarity that makes someone worth learning from.
pali: Kiccho manussapaṭilābho, kicchaṁ maccāna jīvitaṁ; Kicchaṁ saddhammassavanaṁ, kiccho buddhānamuppādo.
translation: Difficult (to obtain) is the conception of men, difficult is the life of mortals, difficult is the hearing of the True Law, difficult is the birth of the Awakened (the attainment of Buddhahood).

chapterSummary: Describes the Buddha's own nature and the kind of clarity that makes someone worth learning from.
pali: Sabbapāpassa akaraṇaṁ, kusalassa upasampadā; Sacittapariyodapanaṁ, etaṁ buddhāna sāsanaṁ.
translation: Not to commit any sin, to do good, and to purify one's mind, that is the teaching of (all) the Awakened.

chapterSummary: Describes the Buddha's own nature and the kind of clarity that makes someone worth learning from.
pali: Khantī paramaṁ tapo titikkhā, Nibbānaṁ paramaṁ vadanti buddhā; Na hi pabbajito parūpaghātī, Na samaṇo hoti paraṁ viheṭhayanto.
translation: The Awakened call patience the highest penance, long-suffering the highest Nirvana; for he is not an anchorite (pravragita) who strikes others, he is not an ascetic (sramana) who insults others.

chapterSummary: Describes the Buddha's own nature and the kind of clarity that makes someone worth learning from.
pali: Anūpavādo anūpaghāto, Pātimokkhe ca saṁvaro; Mattaññutā ca bhattasmiṁ, Pantañca sayanāsanaṁ; Adhicitte ca āyogo, Etaṁ buddhāna sāsanaṁ.
translation: Not to blame, not to strike, to live restrained under the law, to be moderate in eating, to sleep and sit alone, and to dwell on the highest thoughts,--this is the teaching of the Awakened.

chapterSummary: Describes the Buddha's own nature and the kind of clarity that makes someone worth learning from.
pali: Na kahāpaṇavassena, titti kāmesu vijjati; Appassādā dukhā kāmā, iti viññāya paṇḍito.
translation: There is no satisfying lusts, even by a shower of gold pieces; he who knows that lusts have a short taste and cause pain, he is wise;

chapterSummary: Describes the Buddha's own nature and the kind of clarity that makes someone worth learning from.
pali: Api dibbesu kāmesu, ratiṁ so nādhigacchati; Taṇhakkhayarato hoti, sammāsambuddhasāvako.
translation: Even in heavenly pleasures he finds no satisfaction, the disciple who is fully awakened delights only in the destruction of all desires.

chapterSummary: Describes the Buddha's own nature and the kind of clarity that makes someone worth learning from.
pali: Bahuṁ ve saraṇaṁ yanti, pabbatāni vanāni ca; Ārāmarukkhacetyāni, manussā bhayatajjitā.
translation: Men, driven by fear, go to many a refuge, to mountains and forests, to groves and sacred trees.

chapterSummary: Describes the Buddha's own nature and the kind of clarity that makes someone worth learning from.
pali: Netaṁ kho saraṇaṁ khemaṁ, netaṁ saraṇamuttamaṁ; Netaṁ saraṇamāgamma, sabbadukkhā pamuccati.
translation: But that is not a safe refuge, that is not the best refuge; a man is not delivered from all pains after having gone to that refuge.

chapterSummary: Describes the Buddha's own nature and the kind of clarity that makes someone worth learning from.
pali: Yo ca buddhañca dhammañca, saṅghañca saraṇaṁ gato; Cattāri ariyasaccāni, sammappaññāya passati.
translation: He who takes refuge with Buddha, the Law, and the Church; he who, with clear understanding, sees the four holy truths:--

chapterSummary: Describes the Buddha's own nature and the kind of clarity that makes someone worth learning from.
pali: Dukkhaṁ dukkhasamuppādaṁ, dukkhassa ca atikkamaṁ; Ariyaṁ caṭṭhaṅgikaṁ maggaṁ, dukkhūpasamagāminaṁ.
translation: Viz. pain, the origin of pain, the destruction of pain, and the eightfold holy way that leads to the quieting of pain;--

chapterSummary: Describes the Buddha's own nature and the kind of clarity that makes someone worth learning from.
pali: Etaṁ kho saraṇaṁ khemaṁ, etaṁ saraṇamuttamaṁ; Etaṁ saraṇamāgamma, sabbadukkhā pamuccati.
translation: That is the safe refuge, that is the best refuge; having gone to that refuge, a man is delivered from all pain.

chapterSummary: Describes the Buddha's own nature and the kind of clarity that makes someone worth learning from.
pali: Dullabho purisājañño, na so sabbattha jāyati; Yattha so jāyati dhīro, taṁ kulaṁ sukhamedhati.
translation: A supernatural person (a Buddha) is not easily found, he is not born everywhere. Wherever such a sage is born, that race prospers.

chapterSummary: Describes the Buddha's own nature and the kind of clarity that makes someone worth learning from.
pali: Sukho buddhānamuppādo, sukhā saddhammadesanā; Sukhā saṅghassa sāmaggī, samaggānaṁ tapo sukho.
translation: Happy is the arising of the awakened, happy is the teaching of the True Law, happy is peace in the church, happy is the devotion of those who are at peace.

chapterSummary: Describes the Buddha's own nature and the kind of clarity that makes someone worth learning from.
pali: Pūjārahe pūjayato, buddhe yadi va sāvake; Papañcasamatikkante, tiṇṇasokapariddave.
translation: He who pays homage to those who deserve homage, whether the awakened (Buddha) or their disciples, those who have overcome the host (of evils), and crossed the flood of sorrow, he who pays homage to such as have found deliverance and know no fear, his merit can never be measured by anybody.

chapterSummary: Describes the Buddha's own nature and the kind of clarity that makes someone worth learning from.
pali: Te tādise pūjayato, nibbute akutobhaye; Na sakkā puññaṁ saṅkhātuṁ, imettamapi kenaci. Buddhavaggo cuddasamo. Paṭhamabhāṇavāraṁ.
translation: He who pays homage to those who deserve homage, whether the awakened (Buddha) or their disciples, those who have overcome the host (of evils), and crossed the flood of sorrow, he who pays homage to such as have found deliverance and know no fear, his merit can never be measured by anybody.

chapterSummary: Defines a durable happiness that has nothing to do with winning or possessing, only with letting go.
pali: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma, verinesu averino; Verinesu manussesu, viharāma averino.
translation: Let us live happily then, not hating those who hate us! among men who hate us let us dwell free from hatred!

chapterSummary: Defines a durable happiness that has nothing to do with winning or possessing, only with letting go.
pali: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma, āturesu anāturā; Āturesu manussesu, viharāma anāturā.
translation: Let us live happily then, free from ailments among the ailing! among men who are ailing let us dwell free from ailments!

chapterSummary: Defines a durable happiness that has nothing to do with winning or possessing, only with letting go.
pali: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma, ussukesu anussukā; Ussukesu manussesu, viharāma anussukā.
translation: Let us live happily then, free from greed among the greedy! among men who are greedy let us dwell free from greed!
