pali: Akakkasaṁ viññāpaniṁ, giraṁ saccamudīraye; Yāya nābhisaje kañci, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who utters true speech, instructive and free from harshness, so that he offend no one.

chapterSummary: Closes by redefining who deserves to be called noble: not birth or ritual, but how a person actually lives.
pali: Yodha dīghaṁ va rassaṁ vā, aṇuṁ thūlaṁ subhāsubhaṁ; Loke adinnaṁ nādiyati, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who takes nothing in the world that is not given him, be it long or short, small or large, good or bad.

chapterSummary: Closes by redefining who deserves to be called noble: not birth or ritual, but how a person actually lives.
pali: Āsā yassa na vijjanti, asmiṁ loke paramhi ca; Nirāsāsaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who fosters no desires for this world or for the next, has no inclinations, and is unshackled.

chapterSummary: Closes by redefining who deserves to be called noble: not birth or ritual, but how a person actually lives.
pali: Yassālayā na vijjanti, aññāya akathaṅkathī; Amatogadhamanuppattaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who has no interests, and when he has understood (the truth), does not say How, how? and who has reached the depth of the Immortal.

chapterSummary: Closes by redefining who deserves to be called noble: not birth or ritual, but how a person actually lives.
pali: Yodha puññañca pāpañca, ubho saṅgamupaccagā; Asokaṁ virajaṁ suddhaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who in this world is above good and evil, above the bondage of both, free from grief from sin, and from impurity.

chapterSummary: Closes by redefining who deserves to be called noble: not birth or ritual, but how a person actually lives.
pali: Candaṁva vimalaṁ suddhaṁ, vippasannamanāvilaṁ; Nandībhavaparikkhīṇaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who is bright like the moon, pure, serene, undisturbed, and in whom all gaiety is extinct.

chapterSummary: Closes by redefining who deserves to be called noble: not birth or ritual, but how a person actually lives.
pali: Yomaṁ palipathaṁ duggaṁ, saṁsāraṁ mohamaccagā; Tiṇṇo pāraṅgato jhāyī, anejo akathaṅkathī; Anupādāya nibbuto, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who has traversed this miry road, the impassable world and its vanity, who has gone through, and reached the other shore, is thoughtful, guileless, free from doubts, free from attachment, and content.

chapterSummary: Closes by redefining who deserves to be called noble: not birth or ritual, but how a person actually lives.
pali: Yodha kāme pahantvāna, anāgāro paribbaje; Kāmabhavaparikkhīṇaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who in this world, leaving all desires, travels about without a home, and in whom all concupiscence is extinct.

chapterSummary: Closes by redefining who deserves to be called noble: not birth or ritual, but how a person actually lives.
pali: Yodha taṇhaṁ pahantvāna, anāgāro paribbaje; Taṇhābhavaparikkhīṇaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ. Jotikattheravatthu Yodha taṇhaṁ pahantvāna, anāgāro paribbaje; Taṇhābhavaparikkhīṇaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who, leaving all longings, travels about without a home, and in whom all covetousness is extinct.

chapterSummary: Closes by redefining who deserves to be called noble: not birth or ritual, but how a person actually lives.
pali: Hitvā mānusakaṁ yogaṁ, dibbaṁ yogaṁ upaccagā; Sabbayogavisaṁyuttaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who, after leaving all bondage to men, has risen above all bondage to the gods, and is free from all and every bondage.

chapterSummary: Closes by redefining who deserves to be called noble: not birth or ritual, but how a person actually lives.
pali: Hitvā ratiñca aratiñca, sītibhūtaṁ nirūpadhiṁ; Sabbalokābhibhuṁ vīraṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who has left what gives pleasure and what gives pain, who is cold, and free from all germs (of renewed life), the hero who has conquered all the worlds.

chapterSummary: Closes by redefining who deserves to be called noble: not birth or ritual, but how a person actually lives.
pali: Cutiṁ yo vedi sattānaṁ, upapattiñca sabbaso; Asattaṁ sugataṁ buddhaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who knows the destruction and the return of beings everywhere, who is free from bondage, welfaring (Sugata), and awakened (Buddha).

chapterSummary: Closes by redefining who deserves to be called noble: not birth or ritual, but how a person actually lives.
pali: Yassa gatiṁ na jānanti, devā gandhabbamānusā; Khīṇāsavaṁ arahantaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana whose path the gods do not know, nor spirits (Gandharvas), nor men, whose passions are extinct, and who is an Arhat (venerable).

chapterSummary: Closes by redefining who deserves to be called noble: not birth or ritual, but how a person actually lives.
pali: Yassa pure ca pacchā ca, majjhe ca natthi kiñcanaṁ; Akiñcanaṁ anādānaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who calls nothing his own, whether it be before, behind, or between, who is poor, and free from the love of the world.

chapterSummary: Closes by redefining who deserves to be called noble: not birth or ritual, but how a person actually lives.
pali: Usabhaṁ pavaraṁ vīraṁ, mahesiṁ vijitāvinaṁ; Anejaṁ nhātakaṁ buddhaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana, the manly, the noble, the hero, the great sage, the conqueror, the impassible, the accomplished, the awakened.

chapterSummary: Closes by redefining who deserves to be called noble: not birth or ritual, but how a person actually lives.
pali: Pubbenivāsaṁ yo vedi, saggāpāyañca passati; Atho jātikkhayaṁ patto, abhiññāvosito muni; Sabbavositavosānaṁ, tamahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
translation: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who knows his former abodes, who sees heaven and hell, has reached the end of births, is perfect in knowledge, a sage, and whose perfections are all perfect.
